name: Leg Press Calf Press
grip: Hands holding side safety handles of the leg press carriage.
description: Perform ankle plantar flexion against the leg press footplate with knees softly extended, emphasizing the gastrocnemius.
setup: Sit firmly in the 45-degree leg press with back and hips supported against the pads.
Place the balls of both feet along the lower edge of the footplate, hip-width apart, with heels free to drop into dorsiflexion.
Extend legs so knees are softly unlocked (never hyperextended) and disengage the safety bars.
instructions: Lower the carriage by allowing your ankles to dorsiflex, letting your heels drop below the footplate edge until you feel a deep calf stretch.
Press through the balls of your feet into full plantar flexion, driving the sled upward with your calves.
Hold the peak contraction at the top for a moment on your toes.
Lower slowly under control back into the full stretch before beginning the next repetition.
cues: Keep knees softly unlocked and motionless.
Press through the balls of the feet.
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the knees to turn the exercise into a leg press.
Hyperextending or locking out the knees under heavy sled load.
Bouncing out of the bottom stretch without control.

logging.example: Four 20 kg plates loaded (two per side): record 80 kg total plate load on sled.
logging.note: 45-degree sleds have an effective load of approximately 70% of plate mass plus carriage weight; record loaded plate mass.

variantNote: Calf press performed on a 45-degree sled leg press machine with straight legs to recruit the gastrocnemius under stretch.
